reason: The cited evidence shows laser-clad HEAs can provide wear-resistant coatings (E1, E3) and notes an absence of a pronounced HAZ in some HEAs (E2), but none of the passages directly support the key premises about hot-cracking suppression, rapid solidification effects on low-melting phases, or mechanical integrity under aggressive service conditions. The evidence is only loosely related to the specific claims.
premises: Laser cladding reduces thermal input and time in the melting range compared to fusion welding
Rapid solidification suppresses low-melting phases that cause hot cracking
Tailored HEA composition can avoid deleterious phase formation and hot cracking
Laser-clad HEA coatings produce a fine, crack-resistant, metallurgically bonded microstructure
The resulting repair layer maintains mechanical integrity under high-stress and high-temperature service
